Plot Batch Comparison Heatmap

Source: R/plot.R
plot_batch_comparison.Rd

Creates a heatmap comparing significance across multiple samples and bandwidths. Useful for visualizing batch processing results.

plot_batch_comparison(
  results,
  value_var = "z_score",
  cluster_rows = TRUE,
  color_low = "#2166AC",
  color_high = "#B2182B",
  na_value = "gray90",
  show_values = FALSE,
  value_size = 3
)

Arguments

results

List of kernelcomm_result objects (from multiScaleAC_batch)

value_var

Character. Which value to plot: "z_score", "p_value", "observed" (default: "z_score")

cluster_rows

Logical. Cluster samples by similarity? (default: TRUE)

color_low

Character. Color for low values (default: blue)

color_high

Character. Color for high values (default: red)

na_value

Character. Color for NA values (default: gray90)

show_values

Logical. Show numeric values in cells? (default: FALSE)

value_size

Numeric. Text size for cell values (default: 3)

Value

ggplot2::ggplot object

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Process multiple samples
data_list <- list(sample1 = ccRCCExample, sample2 = ccRCCExample)
results <- multiScaleAC_batch(data_list, h_vec = c(10, 20, 40), perms = 99)
results <- lapply(results, compute_significance)

# Plot heatmap of z-scores
plot_batch_comparison(results, value_var = "z_score")

# Plot heatmap of p-values
plot_batch_comparison(results, value_var = "p_value")
} # }
